dedupe_keys.name: spaghetti spatial graphs networks topology and inference pysal

description: spaghetti (SPAtial GrapHs: nETworks, Topology, and Inference) is an open-source Python library for the analysis of network-based spatial data, developed within the Python Spatial Analysis Library (PySAL) from its original network module. It builds graph-theoretic networks from line data and uses libpysal spatial weights to create network segment contiguity objects. Coverage: generic. Examples in the documentation cover snapping observations to networks, shortest path visualisation, minimum spanning trees and caveats of network analysis. Format and access: installable from conda-forge (recommended) or PyPI; tested on Python 3.10 or later; tutorials run as interactive binders. Licence and cost: BSD-3-Clause, free. Caveats: an analysis library for network-constrained spatial data, not a traffic assignment or simulation model. It supports network flow studies that need network distances and network-constrained point patterns, such as crash clustering or service catchments on roads. It relates to OSMnx and sDNA in the catalogue.
